messages:
Rae: Heads-up — PolarWave saw a visible p95 token latency bump (~280ms) for 25m during their 10:05-10:30 UTC activation window. Renewal healthcheck in 8 days, want a low-risk perf proposal.
Ethan: Do we have the invocation profile? streaming vs non, typical prompt/resp lengths, peak QPS?
Rae: Non-streaming completion workload, median prompt ~160 tokens, response ~140 tokens, peak parallelism from a nightly sync. No embeddings. QPS steady ~12, spiked to ~48 during the window.
Sofia: Trace sample:
```
[10:12:07] req=zx12 model=redwood/response-v1 seq_in=162 seq_out=138 batch=2 device=gpu-1 p95=610ms
[10:12:09] req=ab34 model=redwood/response-v1 seq_in=158 seq_out=142 batch=8 device=gpu-1 p95=980ms
```
Sofia: Batch=8 clearly correlates with the highest p95. No OOMs but queue latency climbs.
Rae: Proposed conservative runbook: 1) small canary to redwood/efficacy-micro-v1:int4 (10% traffic), 2) apply staged routing with semantic-fingerprint gating (run automated fingerprint diff on 12 canonical templates), 3) split routing 70% Dedicated / 20% Hosted / 10% canary, 4) set SLO target p95 <= baseline+160ms.
Ethan: int4 is more aggressive than usual. We should lock a semantic gate: compute fingerprint similarity threshold >= 0.98 and require no more than 1 human QA failure in the 12-sample set before stepping.
Marta (PolarWave): We need exact phrasing for our public-facing summaries — legal will only approve if we pass their regression and a one-hour shadowed run.
Rae: Plan to run: 1) eval job against customer templates + lexical/semantic diffs (BLEU + embedding-sim), 2) 1h shadowed traffic where we log A/B outputs (no user-facing change), 3) then enable 10% canary, monitor 30m windows, step to 40% if stable. Rollback triggers: p95 > baseline+160ms for 10m OR semantic_fingerprint < 0.98 OR human_failures >=1.
Sofia: Ops tweaks: reduce continuous_batch_size_limit for their dedicated pool from 64 -> 40 for the canary window, set KV-prefetch TTL=90s to avoid thrash, and enable proto-kv-compact mode to reduce memory footprint under int4. Also pre-warm top-25 prefixes.
Ethan: Add autoscale_headroom 0.30 on the dedicated pool during the canary and reserve +1 GPU for the first 3 hours. Also enable detailed A/B logging retention for 7 days.
Rae: Draft route config for approval:
```
route: polarwave-int4-staged
- match: customer_id == "polarwave"
- weights: {dedicated: 70, hosted: 20, canary: 10}
- canary_model: redwood/efficacy-micro-v1:int4
- autoscale_headroom: 0.30
- continuous_batch_size_limit: 40
- kv_prefetch_ttl_s: 90
- semantic_gate: {fingerprint_threshold: 0.98, sample_count: 12}
- rollback_policy: {p95_delta_ms: 160, eval_window_m: 10}
```
Marta (PolarWave): Shadowed run + eval set sign-off needed. Can QA join the 15:30 UTC run?
Rae: Yes — scheduling 15:30 UTC shadow run and 16:15 quick check-in for QA verdict.
ops-bot: Canary job created: polarwave-int4-4765432100; monitors=[p95_tokens, error_rate, semantic_fingerprint]; auto-revert conditions set: p95>baseline+160ms for 10m OR semantic_fingerprint<0.98 OR human_failed_samples>=1 -> route_revert_to:redwood/response-v1
Ethan: One more note — include an automatic difflog that highlights token-level edits and punctuation shifts to help QA focus. Keep difflog retention 7 days.
Marta (PolarWave): Good. If the canary passes and paperwork is satisfied we are open to a longer migration to the micro model for cost savings.
Rae: Action items: Rae prepare evalset + invite QA, Sofia implement pool limits and pre-warm, Ethan reserve GPU + enable logs, ops-bot run canary and auto-revert. Will post results here after shadow + 1h of canary. :white_check_mark:
